chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Kansas City and Minneapolis music scenes
summary: Kansas City and Minneapolis were great towns; Frank Hine's big band had Lester Young and Eddie Barefield and trumpeter Rook Gands.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. In Kansas City where that was. Man, that's the damnedest town in the United States. And Minneapolis was also.
It was good in Minneapolis, too.

Yeah, it was good in Minneapolis. They had old Frank Hine played as much piano as Earl Hines! Sure did. Yeah, he had a hell of a big band with Lester Young, and Eddie Barefield was in it. Rook(?) Gands, had that five-valve(?) trumpet. He still did.
I never heard of him. I remember a trumpet player named Roy Gaines. No, Charlie Gaines. There used to be a trumpet player called Charlie Gaines. Did you ever hear him?
Maybe he just worked out of New York.
No, Rook(?)... He's right up there. He's doing

work with this organ player by the name of...they call him Buster. He comes down through here every year. He has a ...(?)... of Texas, and he comes through here with Rook(?), and they play gigs together all the time there in Minneapolis.
